reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in formulating deferral as a joint classification-rejection task, where the system learns to route each instance to either the model or the expert based on conditional correctness probabilities. The cost-sensitive generalized cross-entropy surrogate ensures convexity and Bayes consistency, enabling optimal routing without explicit modeling of expert error rates. The system loss decomposes into model and expert components, allowing for end-to-end training. Instance-dependent expert error modeling via P(expert correct | x) allows the system to defer only when the expert is expected to outperform the model. This formulation supports dynamic routing policies that adapt to input distributions and expert competence variations. The method avoids reliance on fixed thresholds or confidence scores, instead learning adaptive deferral boundaries directly from training data. In GSE, this translates to a state transition engine that dynamically selects between model prediction, expert deferment, and abstention based on learned uncertainty and reliability signals.
